newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Babcock shares up as board meets.
newsitem.headline: D.Babcock shares up as board meets.

text.p: Shares in German engineering and plant construction group Deutsche Babcock AG were up sharply in mid-morning trading ahead of a key supervisory board meeting that could decide the fate of the embattled chairman.

The supervisory board was expected to release preliminary earnings figures for the business year that ended on September 30, 1996 and there was mounting speculation that chairman Heyo Schmiedeknecht could be dismissed at the board meeting.

While dealers said they were not paying special attention to the stock, Babcock shares were up over eight percent by 1120 GMT at 70 marks ($43.06), a rise of 5.50 marks from Friday on the Frankfurt stock exchange.
The company's shares have been rising after a free fall of over a year because of its unsuccessful attempts to restructure and regain profitability.
According to German press reports at the weekend, Babcock's supervisory board planned to dismiss Schmiedeknecht for failing to turn the company around.
After several restructuring attempts, Babcock's management in mid-1996 devised a reorganisation for which the company's banks provided a credit line of about 600 million marks until the end of 1997.
But the news weekly Der Spiegel said in its latest issue that Schmiedeknecht last October reported a new liquidity gap of 100 million marks.

At that time Babcock had rejected growing speculation that it was insolvent and said its core businesses would be profitable in 1995/96, but that it would still post a loss of some 400 million marks for the year.

The reorganisation was expected to include the sale of 20 of the company's 60 subsidiaries, but analysts said at the time that the efforts were proceeding too slowly and restructuring charges were likely to be higher than expected.

Schmiedeknecht took the helm at Babcock in May 1990 at a time when the company's reliance on plant making for the energy sector drove the group into the red. He launched a programme to diversify the company's business.
A spokeswoman for Deutsche Babcock contacted by Reuters declined to confirm the reports and said that Monday's board meeting was routine.
Spiegel said Schmiedeknecht had come under fire for purchasing companies which were now making losses.
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.625 German Marks)
